person.name: Sahand Sharifzadeh
person.eyebrow: Staff Research Scientist · Gemini · Google DeepMind, London
lead: Building frontier multimodal and reasoning models across 12+ years of research in foundation models, computer vision, deep RL, and robotics.

I drove the co-development and validation of a key recipe used in Gemini 4 series (Argon, Carbon) and contributed to the Gemini 2 and 3 model series and Flamingo. Across Gemini Mid-Training and Thinking, my research has spanned reinforcement learning efficiency and scaling, inference-time scaling, quantization in post-training, and strategic reasoning in games. I also co-led research on self-improving VLMs.

Earlier, my research spanned looped graph transformers for iterative scene understanding (Classification by Attention, 2020), knowledge graph embeddings (PyKEEN), and deep inverse reinforcement learning for autonomous driving.
person.description: Sahand Sharifzadeh is a Staff Research Scientist on the Gemini team at Google DeepMind in London, working on mid-training, reasoning and multimodal models.
person.contact: The best way to reach me is a message on LinkedIn or X.
keyFacts: Developed a key recipe used in Gemini 4 Argon as a core member of the Gemini Mid-Training team; contributed to the Gemini 2 and 3 model series.
Contributed to Flamingo (NeurIPS 2022) as a DeepMind research scientist intern in 2021; first author and co-lead of Synth² (2024).
Ph.D. in Computer Science, summa cum laude, LMU Munich (supervisor: Prof. Volker Tresp); M.Sc. TU Munich; B.Sc. Shahid Beheshti University.

news.text: Gemini 4 Argon is now available to everyone, after its announcement on 30 September. I was a core member of the Gemini Mid-Training team and developed a key recipe used in the model.
Game Arena: strategic LLM evaluation in competitive environments (Kaggle). Technical report on arXiv.
Synth²: self-improving VLMs with synthetic captions and image embeddings (co-lead).
Ultra-high-granularity detector simulation published in Nature Communications.

blog.title: A Looped Transformer for Scene Understanding, Six Years Later
blog.description: Explore looped Transformers through Classification by Attention (2020): shared weights, schema feedback, and a precise comparison with Meta’s looped LLM research.
blog.summary: An interactive retrospective on Classification by Attention (2020), a looped graph Transformer for visual scene understanding, not an LLM. Explains weight-shared four-layer stack reuse, prediction-mediated schema feedback, original-image-feature reinjection, detached feedback during training, and evaluation with more passes than training. Compares these mechanisms with FAIR at Meta’s How to Loop Your Transformer (2026), distinguishing stack reuse and input anchoring from hidden-state recurrence, loop-specific adapters and cross-token parallel decoding. Credits Universal Transformers (2018); makes no absolute first claim or claim of direct influence. Includes a plain-language loop overview and measured per-assimilation SGCls recall curves reconstructed approximately from original Figure 4; marks the four-pass training boundary and evaluation up to eight passes. Cross-method mean recall is optional historical context, not the main evidence for looping.
